about: Hardware checks a stable release needs (ops/ship/hwgate.py). Code merges never wait for them. A capability applies when one of its `present` probes matches the commit: a file glob, then a regex searched in each matching file. Every `require` check of an applying capability needs a `pass` for that build. A pull request that adds or changes a device capability, or a device-side file, updates this file in the same pull request.

checks.shared-receiver: Keyboard and mouse on one Bolt receiver: both found; a remapped key works during a mouse gesture.
checks.mixed-connections: Keyboard on Bluetooth with the mouse on Bolt, then both on Bluetooth: both found, remapped keys work.
checks.service-stop-restores-keys: Remap a key, then stop the user service: the key does its own function again.
checks.crash-recovery: Kill the app with SIGKILL while a key is remapped: key state noted; restart recovers it; state after a keyboard power cycle noted.
checks.easy-switch-away: Press the keyboard's Easy-Switch key to a computer without MX Options while a key is remapped: note whether the key works natively there or is dead.
checks.sleep-wake: Sleep and wake the computer: remapped keys work again.
checks.receiver-replug: Unplug and replug the receiver with both devices on it: both found again, remapped keys work.
checks.keyboard-battery: Keyboard battery level shown; the low-battery notice appears.
checks.top-row-fn-modes: Fn+Esc in both modes: note which control IDs a remapped top-row key reports.
checks.bluetooth-zero-id-access: Keyboard attached over Bluetooth with a zero product ID: note the access result; no udev rule change.
checks.windows-keyboard: Windows 11 with Logi Options+ stopped: keyboard found; remap, restore and held keys behave.
checks.shared-receiver-mouse-latency: Mouse request latency while the keyboard is probed on a shared receiver, measured from the debug log.
checks.keyboard-identity: Keyboard identity read with a non-zero unit ID; same over Bolt and Bluetooth and after a power cycle; differs between two units when two are available. Identifiers stay in private notes, never in the evidence record.
checks.mouse-follows-keyboard: Mouse-follows-keyboard on, press the keyboard's Easy-Switch key: the mouse moves to the same computer; latency noted; mouse-in-deep-sleep case noted; three-computer case.
checks.keyboard-follow-held-key-check: Keyboard follows the mouse over Flow: with no key held it follows; holding Shift, a letter key, or a media key not set to an app action, it stays; each direction and connection noted. From a Windows computer it stays (unsupported): there the keyboard's Easy-Switch key brings it back.
checks.keyboard-follow-held-key-at-switch: Hold a key physically during an Easy-Switch: note what the old and the new computer see.
checks.keyboard-follow-two-computers: Two Linux computers paired over Flow: the keyboard follows the mouse both ways, keys given back before the switch, no dead keys, 40 crossings in one session.
checks.app-profiles-desktops: Keyboard app profiles change keys for the app in front on KDE Wayland, X11, sway, Hyprland and Windows; GNOME shows the not-available message.
checks.fn-lock-setting: Toggle the Fn lock switch: the top row flips. The keyboard's own Fn-lock shortcut: the switch follows within a second. Easy-Switch away and back: setting kept per channel as the keyboard keeps it. Power cycle: kept. Toggle while holding F5 with the mouse, then release: no stuck key.
checks.disable-keys-setting: Disable and enable each advertised key; rapid changes preserve both choices. Check power cycle, a native modifier held during change, and a remapped key. Restore earlier disable setting first, then press and release any stuck modifier on original computer.
checks.os-layout-setting: Change layout on current channel and read it back; check keyboard shortcut, remapped keys and a held native modifier. Restore earlier layout first, then press and release affected modifier on original computer. Record other-channel behavior when available.
checks.backlight-settings: Exercise every enabled backlight control and each timer; read-only or unsupported controls stay disabled. Check keyboard brightness keys and notices, own-change suppression, power cycle and preserved settings. Record unsupported controls without claiming them implemented.
checks.backlight-effect-ids-observed: Choose each backlight effect with the keyboard's own effect key and run tools/hidpp_probe.py --json after each: the effect byte read back equals the ID this build names for the effect the keyboard shows, for every effect, the same over two full cycles. Any mismatch is a fail; effects then stay a hint.
checks.lock-key-notices: Turn lock-key notices on: Caps Lock and Num Lock toggles show the right notice; off shows nothing.
